attributes.title: Far match
attributes.sample:
{{! Three bays, three regions. A region reconciles its OWN participants and nothing else — that is what makes nesting work, and it is why a piece leaving one and arriving in another is normally a death here and an unrelated birth there. Every region that will animate this pass announces while Glimmer is still rendering. Then all of them MEASURE, then ids are MATCHED across regions, then each RUNs its own timeline. Three phases, no frame in between. }} {{#each bays as |bay|}}
{{#each (this.piecesIn bay.id) key='id' as |piece|}} {{! the same bare id in every bay is what lets the barrier pair the two halves. Prefixing it with the bay is the whole of ‘off’. }} {{/each}}
{{! One rule covers both halves, because to a region they are the same job: every piece that is somewhere new moves there. A neighbour closing a gap has a small delta; a piece that arrived from another bay has the delta between two bays — and only because the barrier handed it the sender’s bounds to start from. }} {{! a property may be a function of the sprite, and ‘did you come from another region’ is exactly what counterpart answers }} {{! with matching on, neither of these fires: the sender is let go quietly by its own region, and the receiver is kept, not inserted }} {{/each}} const layer = (sprite) => (sprite.counterpart ? 6 : 1);

lesson.concept: Identity can cross a region boundary
lesson.why: A matching bare id leaving one region and arriving in another pairs across the render pass. The receiver carries the previous bounds, while each region retains its own scene ownership.
lesson.experiment: Move an item between bays and interrupt the flight. Toggle matching to compare one continuous move with separate removal and insertion.
lesson.pitfall: Prefixing the id with the region name prevents the cross-region identity match.
lesson.combine: Combine with beacons for toolbar destinations that are locations rather than receiving items.
